liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (2 reviews): Jerry plays the opening Jack Straw with an aggressive attack, signaling a hot night; Strong opener, described as intense and lyrical [21][28]
- **Franklin's Tower** (2 reviews): Jerry is shaky, perhaps getting only three verses right, and Bobby steps in on mic to rescue it; Jerry forgets nearly all the words [26][27]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): The China Cat into Rider was a nice surprise and a highlight for the reviewer [27]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): A third set started with Althea, and Minglewood in that set struck the reviewer as odd [22]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Brought back during this run after a couple of years unplayed, but played on three of five nights [22]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 other source): Not Fade Away, Stella Blue and Sunshine Daydream are marked with an asterisk in the notes; encore was Good Lovin' [1]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer's personal favorite; played tremendously [28]

## The recordings

- **gd79-12-31.rolfe.vernon.18589.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 26 songs; 220 min; rated 4.25/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: Excellent audience recording balancing crowd energy and playing; during Stella Blue it feels like standing on the arena floor; Fine audience recording by Steve Rolfe, consistent with his other audience tapes from late 1979; Audience tape captures the feeling of being in the room; the reviewer calls it stellar [18][20][21]
- **gd1979-12-31.144796.fob.sony.ecm270.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 26 songs; 225 min [2]
- **gd1979-12-31.sonyecm-walker.walker-scotton-miller.88768.flac16**: source not stated; 27 songs; 221 min; rated 3.71/5 by 7 [4]. Said about its sound: Fine audience recording by Joani Walker; Phil's big bass notes are captured superbly [25]
- **gd1979-12-31.154882.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 26 songs; 209 min [7]
- **gd79-12-31.sbd.hinko.17281.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 207 min; rated 3.5/5 by 8 [12]. Said about its sound: Sounds somewhat fuzzy for a soundboard-sourced matrix recording, falling short of the reviewer's expectations; Matrix sound is only okay [17][23]

## Around the show

- The West Coast crowd is attentive rather than rowdy; there are some vocal flubs in the performance [18]
- Some minor vocal flubs and messy playing, but the band sounds like they're having fun jamming [21]
- Reviewer held a ticket but missed the New Year's Eve show due to a bad case of flu [25]
- Balloon pops and hand claps are heard throughout, especially at the start of the second set, as typical of New Year's [2]
- John Cipollina plays guitar on Not Fade Away, Stella Blue and Sunshine Daydream [2]
- Reviewer, who attended the run, found this the least inspired night; the second night was remembered as the hottest [22]
- Three sets with unusual transitions and songs rarely played that year, but the show itself is far from excellent [23]
- First and second sets are fairly well played but uninspired; band neither dazzles nor disappoints [25]
- Reviewer felt the band had an off night with low energy throughout, despite New Year's Eve [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd79-12-31.rolfe.vernon.18589.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Rolfe; source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Recorded by Steve Rolfe on Nakamichi 700s via Dave Minor, then to D5, DAT and CDR; encoded and patched by Matt Vernon [1]
- **gd1979-12-31.144796.fob.sony.ecm270.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM-270 mics (stand mounted, 35' from stage, several feet left of the free throw circle)> Sony TC-D5… [2]
- **gd1979-12-31.sonyecm-walker.walker-scotton-miller.88768.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sony ECM-250 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-158/Maxell UDXL-II90) [4]. Also: Walker and Scotton tapes; the Rolfe Nakamichi 700 CD source supplies patches, including a seamless disc change between Set 3 and encore [4]
- **gd1979-12-31.154882.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [7]
- **gd79-12-31.sbd.hinko.17281.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [12]. Also: Matrix source; the full show fits on three discs by combining disc 3 track 2 through disc 4 track 4 [17]

Master cassettes from Mark Severson, transferred by Charlie Miller; Sony ECM-270 source; 0:08 patch in Drums from the Rolfe/Vernon tape
Walker and Scotton tapes; the Rolfe Nakamichi 700 CD source supplies patches, including a seamless disc change between Set 3 and encore
Source cassettes and transfer by Scott Wiseman on AKG; a 0:29 patch in Drums comes from Severson's Sony ECM-270 source
